Subject: Post-call: EdgeFin performance qualification — recap & next steps

Alex,

Thanks for the time today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap
- Candidate workload: interactive risk-analysis chat and batch report generation (mix of short and long context).
- Target SLOs you mentioned: 95th p99 latency < 300ms for streaming replies for short queries; tail p99 (non-stream) < 800ms for long-context generation; sustained throughput target ~120 reqs/sec with occasional spikes to 250 reqs/sec.
- Concurrency: expected 80 concurrent active sessions for peak.
- Streaming: token-by-token streaming required for the UI; need <150ms first-byte for short replies.

Immediate next steps
1) Please share a representative prompt set + a few synthetic long-context cases (can be redacted).
2) We'll send our benchmark methodology (measurement defs, harness, reproducibility checklist) and propose a run plan (remote vs in-person).
3) Align on success criteria and pass/fail thresholds for the pilot.

I'll attach a short checklist and the SLO template we discussed. Marcus and Dylan are looped to scope the benchmark run and estimate run time/cost.

If you can send the prompt set and a few sample payloads by EOD Monday (6/28), we can schedule an initial remote run the week of 7/5.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Benchmark methodology and measurement definitions (draft)

Alex — received, thanks. Below is the benchmark methodology we propose; sharing here so you can review and flag any gaps. We'll also upload a formal spec to the Drive folder.

Benchmark methodology (summary)
- Harness: we use an automated harness that replays the provided prompt set against the candidate model(s) under controlled concurrency and arrival patterns. We support both synchronous and streaming modes.
- Measurement windows: warmup of 2 minutes, then a 10-minute measured window per configuration. We can extend windows for longer stability checks.
- Metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, throughput (reqs/sec), tokens/sec, first-byte latency for streaming (FBT), error rate, and CPU/GPU utilization.
- Tail/streaming definitions:
  - p99 latency (non-stream): 99th percentile of end-to-end response completion time per request.
  - Streaming FBT: time to first non-empty chunk (ms). Target: p95 FBT <150ms for short queries.
  - Measured token throughput: total model-side generated tokens / measured second.
- Concurrency patterns: we will replay realistic inter-arrival times based on your CSV; peak concurrency will be tested explicitly (80 and 150 concurrent sessions).
- Reproducibility: each run will include a run-id and a hash of the prompt set + harness version. We fix RNG seeds where applicable and record model checkpoints + quantization profile, runtime kernel selection, and environment (instance type, driver versions). Runs are archived in the Drive folder with logs and raw traces.

Pass/fail guidance (proposed)
- Green: p99 (streaming) < 300ms OR p99 (non-stream) < 800ms AND sustained throughput >= 120 reqs/sec with <1% error rate.
- Yellow: within 10% of targets or requires minor infra tuning.
- Red: misses both latency and throughput targets by >20%.

Data handling and artifacts
- We will not store your prompts beyond the run if you request redaction; we can also run exclusively on your private deployment if preferred.
- Deliverables: raw logs, aggregated metrics, flamegraphs for hot kernels, and a short report with recommended tuning (batching, quant profiles, routing).

Proposed next steps
1) Can you confirm the CSV includes representative arrival patterns? If not, please add inter-arrival times.
2) Do you prefer we run the initial test against our hosted environment, or against a private deployment (customer-managed)? Hosted is faster to iterate.
3) If hosted: please provide an allowlisted test token (expires after runs) and confirm any IP allowlisting for our test harness.

Marcus and Dylan — can you review the resources needed (approx GPU-hours) and propose a tentative run schedule?

Best,
Marissa
